title: SOC2 timeline probe — evidence triage and quick wins
body:
Top-level goal: identify 2-week evidence sprint that yields most auditable controls for SOC2 Type 1 probe.

Context and constraints:
- We're in early prep for Type 1; primary ask from auditor is control design + evidence that controls are implemented (where applicable).
- Hosted API customers vs Private (VPC/on-prem) have different artefacts; focus initial sprint on hosted infra because evidence is easier to centralize.
- Major risk areas flagged by security review: KMS key custody procedures (private), deployment change approvals, incident alerting -> ticketing linkage.

Quick wins (target first 10 business days):
1) Access logs + admin activity exports
   - Owner: Marta
   - Artefact: daily admin audit CSV from console (last 90 days) + how-to doc
   - Why: demonstrates lookup/monitoring control (common SOC question).
   - TODO: script to pull most recent 90 days and checksum; attach to Confluence.
2) RBAC mapping snapshot + policy doc
   - Owner: Noah
   - Artefact: IAM roles list + sample user role assignment + one approval email chain
   - Why: shows that role separation exists and approvals are recorded.
3) Change control evidence for model rollouts
   - Owner: Ivy (me) + Eng lead on serving-runtime
   - Artefacts: PR -> rollout runbook -> canary metric snapshot -> rollback note if any
   - Minimal acceptance criteria: a PR and runbook snapshot for at least one model rollout in last 6 months.

Control mapping notes (working matrix, rough):
- CC: Logical access (AC-1, AC-2 analogs) -> evidence: IAM list, access reviews, SSO config export
- CC: Change management -> evidence: PR history + deployment windows + approval ticket
- CC: Incident response -> evidence: 1 pager IR plan + one incident ticket with timeline and comms
- CC: Encryption & key mgmt -> evidence: KMS policy, key rotation schedule, HSM/KMS owner email threads

Open questions / blockers:
- Private deployments: customers manage their own KMS in most cases. Auditor asks for "how customers ensure keys are rotated" — we currently have guidance but no enforcement. Action: scope this out as "documentation control" (not enforced).
- Do we have a single canonical place for IE logs? SRE says logs are scattered between cluster-managed stacks and a central logging endpoint. Need an aggregation plan for auditable exports.
- Evidence retention windows: Product says 180 days for some telemetry; auditor may ask for 12 months depending on control. Need to confirm target retention policy.

Automation ideas (low-effort, high-impact):
- Small lambda job to snapshot IAM/roles weekly and drop into secure folder with checksum + timestamp. Generates historical evidence for access review.
- Hook in CI to tag PRs that are security-relevant (label: security-control-evidence) and auto-snapshot PR diff + approvers to evidence store.

Sample checklist for a single control (change mgmt):
- PR exists: yes/no
- PR approver: name + timestamp
- Rollout runbook: doc link
- Post-rollout metrics: screenshot or csv (latency/correctness)
- Rollback note if executed: ticket reference
- Stored in evidence repo: path

Slack/conversation references (for traceability):
- #eng-release thread: "rollout model x -> canary green" (2026-01-18) (link pinned to Confluence)
- DM from @sre-lead confirming log retention (2026-02-05)

Short-term ask for SRE/Infra this week:
- One-off export: produce a zipped package with admin audit logs + a sample model rollout PR + canary metrics snapshot (target: by Fri 2026-02-20).
- Confirm where we can programmatically pull IAM snapshots (API endpoint and credentials) and whether snapshotting is allowed under current perms.

Evidence packaging format (proposal):
- ZIP named {control-short}-{YYYYMMDD}-{owner}.zip containing:
  - metadata.txt (control, owner, tool versions, hash)
  - artifacts/ (PRs/docs/csvs/screenshots)
  - provenance.txt (who pulled, when, how)

Risks to call out to auditor proactively:
- Private deployments: control design differs; we will provide guidance but cannot attest to customers' on-prem configuration.
- KMS enforcement: internal docs only; no technical enforcement on customers.
- Log centralization gaps may cause missing historical artifacts for very old incidents. Plan: be transparent, provide compensating controls (e.g., monitoring alerts + metrics).

Next actions (this doc as working checklist):
- [ ] Sync with Marta on admin log export script (due 2026-02-18)
- [ ] Ask SRE to run one IAM snapshot and place in evidence repo (due 2026-02-19)
- [ ] Draft short control narrative for change mgmt and attach sample PR (due 2026-02-21)
- [ ] Create evidence ZIP template + upload to Confluence (due 2026-02-22)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep this doc short and actionable. Auditor will want breadcrumbs (who, when, how) more than long policy prose.
- Avoid overpromising on private deploys; offer a professional services checklist instead.
- Later: map these quick wins into the SOC control matrix (longer task).

If we get pushback from Eng about snapshotting credentials: propose read-only role that can list and export, audited by proof-of-use.

End of scratchpad.

(Will iterate: add direct artifact links once exports are available.)
